clue.text: Icebergs, ultimately, repeatedly melt

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Icebergs

parts.note: something done repeatedly is done often

explanation.surface: Icebergs keep melting again and again, a picture of a warming polar sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To melt something is to make it soft, a close synonym of the verb in its loosening sense.

clue.text: Looked for variety in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a variety is a sort or kind

explanation.surface: Someone seeking some variety in their chat.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation, without the R sounded, the word for kind sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sought is the past tense of seek, so it means searched for.

clue.text: Send on attacking player

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to send mail on to a new address
second meaning: a striker in football or rugby

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a manager bringing on a substitute striker; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for passing post along and a noun for a team member who plays up front.

clue.text: Club losing wickets, and advantage

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away

parts.note: a wedge is a type of golf club
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wickets

explanation.surface: A cricket club losing wickets yet still holding the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a cricket club given the wickets, but it is the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over a rival means having a slight advantage.

clue.text: Jack, with mates at sea, discarded goods

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of mates are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack and his shipmates throw cargo overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard from a ship to lighten it, goods deliberately discarded.

clue.text: Exploit unusually large survey of voters

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of exploit are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A warning about misusing an unusually big poll of the electorate.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit poll is a survey of voters taken as they leave the polling station.

clue.text: Band grabbing time in store

indicators.note: grabbing means holding the time letter inside

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist

explanation.surface: A pop band grabbing some time in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians and 'store' a shop, but they are a strip of cloth and a hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something is to store or hide it away for later.

clue.text: A boy enthralled by my affliction

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive by, so these letters sit inside my

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A lovesick admirer describes a boy captivated by them as their affliction.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness or ailment, something that afflicts a person.

clue.text: Winning suitable post

parts.note: a team that is winning is up, ahead in the game
suitable means right, appropriate

explanation.surface: Someone is winning a suitable job or position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' reads as a job, but here it is a vertical pole.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright is a vertical post or pole, such as either side of a goal frame.

clue.text: Learner inside becoming keen on lecture

indicators.note: inside says the learner letter goes within the phrase for becoming keen on

parts.note: taking to someone means becoming keen on them
L is the learner-driver abbreviation

explanation.surface: A student indoors who has begun to enjoy a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding or reprimand, a lecture in the telling-off sense.

clue.text: Popular, a couple of lines taken together

parts.note: something popular is in, fashionable
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL

explanation.surface: A poem that is popular, with a couple of its lines considered as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total or altogether, counting everything as a whole.

clue.text: Pick up her article within

indicators.note: within means the article is placed inside the letters of her

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone collects a woman's item from inside a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' suggests collecting, but here it means catching a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a sound or a piece of news is to catch it with the ears.

clue.text: Sloppy fielders keep dropping Lancashire's opener

parts.note: slips are close catching fielding positions in cricket, beside the wicketkeeper

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is taken out of the word for keep

parts.note: to keep something is to hold it

indicators.note: the opener of Lancashire's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cricket report: careless slip fielders keep dropping catches off Lancashire's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is an English county with a cricket team; L dropped from HOLD leaves HOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is careless and untidy, the same as sloppy.

clue.text: Easiest swimming round island, in my opinion

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the island letter
swimming suggests letters moving about, so easiest is rearranged

parts.note: I is the map abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone's view that the easiest swim is a lap round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom that introduces a personal view, the same as saying what I think.

clue.text: One yet to be adopted by the German company making spirits

indicators.note: adopted by says these letters are taken in by the German word, placed inside it

parts.note: DER is a German word for the
I is the Roman numeral for one
yet means still, as in 'still to come'

explanation.surface: A child still waiting to be adopted by a German business that makes alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller is a firm producing whisky, gin and other distilled liquors.

clue.text: Withdraw religious education pamphlet

parts.note: RE is the school-subject abbreviation for religious education
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: An instruction to recall a religious pamphlet from schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back, to withdraw it.

clue.text: Modify top of dress during a fitting

indicators.note: during means the letter falls within the other pieces

parts.note: fitting means just, fair and appropriate

indicators.note: the top of dress is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tailor alters the top of a dress during a fitting session.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to alter it slightly, a synonym of modify.

clue.text: Lack of interest in a course beginning in York

parts.note: a path is a course or route

indicators.note: the beginning of York is its first letter

explanation.surface: Nobody shows any interest in a course starting in York.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathy is indifference, an absence of enthusiasm or concern.

clue.text: With costume, time for equestrian event

parts.note: a costume can be a dress
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Riders wearing costume at the right time for a horse show.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is a competitive discipline in horse riding where the horse performs precise movements.

clue.text: Best section of thoroughfare, lit extensively

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The finest stretch of a main road, with plenty of street lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best or most select group of people.

clue.text: Employing last of googlies, spinner gets close

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of googlies

parts.note: a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler using googlies comes close to taking a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: A googly is a deceptive delivery by a cricket spin bowler, so 'spinner' looks like the bowler; it is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: To close something down is to end it, a synonym of the verb meaning halt.

clue.text: Celebrity set off, last out

indicators.note: last out says the final letter is removed

parts.note: to start is to set off on a journey

explanation.surface: A famous person sets off, the last to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, a celebrity.

clue.text: Join military group heading for Edinburgh

parts.note: a unit is a military group

indicators.note: the heading of Edinburgh is its first letter

explanation.surface: An invitation to enlist in an army unit bound for Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to bring them together, which is to join them.

clue.text: Exile unconscious in front of shed

indicators.note: in front of says the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: someone knocked unconscious is out
to shed is to cast off, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: A banished man found knocked out in front of a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden building but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile, as a person, is one banished or rejected by society, which is an outcast.

clue.text: Deal with Italy, finally making pact

parts.note: to deal with something is to treat it

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of Italy

explanation.surface: Negotiating with Italy, and at last agreeing a pact.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal agreement between nations, which is a pact.

clue.text: Quite attractive

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as an adverb, fairly or rather
second meaning: as an adjective, good-looking

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'fairly good-looking', but each word is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as an adverb meaning fairly and as an adjective meaning lovely to look at.
